title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts & API Examples — Docs Site Operating Procedures and Top Support Issues Playbook
author: Maya Thompson
body:
Purpose:
Provide a single, operational playbook for Developer Experience (DevEx) owners and contributors that covers: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, canonical API examples, docs site operating procedures, and the top support issues together with canonical fixes. This document is intended for engineers, developer advocates, technical writers, and support engineers who create or maintain user-facing DevEx content.

Scope:
- Public-facing and internal SDK guides (Python, Node, Go, Java)
- Quickstarts and repo templates used in tutorials and onboarding
- Canonical API examples and sample apps maintained in the docs repo
- Docs site publishing, review, and release procedures
- Top support issues observed in Q3 2025 — Q1 2026 and their canonical fixes

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary owner: DevEx Docs (eng-developer-experience)
- Day-to-day maintainers: Docs engineers + SDK champions per language
- Escalation path: Docs engineer -> SDK owner -> Runtime team (eng-serving-runtime) -> SRE (eng-sre)
- Response SLA for high-severity doc regressions: 24 hours

Document types and templates (convention):
1) SDK Guide (long-form):
   - Purpose: comprehensive reference for SDK usage, auth patterns, error handling, and migration notes.
   - Filename pattern: sdk-<language>-guide-YYYY.json (e.g., sdk-python-guide-2026.json)
   - Required sections: Intro, Quickstart, Auth, Usage Examples, Pagination/Streaming, Retry semantics, Troubleshooting, Changelog

2) Quickstart / Tutorial (task-oriented):
   - Purpose: short path to "Hello World" or a single outcome (embed, chat, fine-tune, rerank).
   - Filename pattern: quickstart-<capability>-<language>-YYYY.json
   - Required sections: Prereqs, Step-by-step, Expected output, Local run commands, Deploy / Next steps

3) API Examples (snippet bundle):
   - Purpose: canonical examples used on the API reference (multi-language parity).
   - Filename pattern: api-examples-<endpoint>-YYYY.json
   - Content: 3-4 language blocks (Python, Node, Go, curl) with minimal but copy-paste runnable code.

4) Docs Site SOP (operational):
   - Purpose: publishing, CI checks, release notes, and rollback procedures for docs site content.
   - Filename pattern: docs-site-ops-YYYY.json

5) Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes:
   - Purpose: living list used by support/SEs to triage and fix docs, SDKs, and examples quickly.
   - Filename pattern: top-support-issues-devex-YYYY.json

SDK guide checklist (must-have before marking as published):
- [ ] Auth examples present for API Key and OAuth flows (if applicable)
- [ ] One quickstart (runnable) included and smoke-tested in CI
- [ ] Error handling section with sample retry logic and idempotency guidance
- [ ] Versioning and upgrade notes included for breaking changes
- [ ] Inline code passes linter and language-specific CI jobs
- [ ] Labels: language tag, capability tag, stability tag (stable/beta/experimental)

Quickstart templates (standard structure):
1) Header metadata block (title, description, prerequisites, estimated time)
2) Repository scaffold (files to create, package.json / pyproject.toml example)
3) Step-by-step commands (copy-paste CLI)
4) Expected output block (console + snippets of generated content)
5) Troubleshooting section (2-3 common failure modes)
6) Cleanup instructions and next steps

Example Quickstart (embedding — Python):
- Prereqs: Python 3.10+, pip, API key in REDWOOD_API_KEY
- Install: pip install redwood-sdk
- main.py:
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  import os
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
  resp = client.embeddings.create(model='open-embed-002', input=['hello', 'world'])
  print(resp[0])
- Run: python main.py
- Expected output: JSON array of two embedding vectors (float list)

API examples guidance (best practices):
- Provide multi-language parity for the most commonly used endpoints: chat/completions, embeddings, streaming, and function-calling.
- Keep examples minimal: show auth, request, and response parsing in <= 12 lines per language.
- Where appropriate, include a curl example first for quick verification.
- Avoid SDK wrapper magic in the canonical snippet; prefer explicit, educational examples.

Docs site operating procedures (publishing workflow):
1) Author creates or updates JSON doc in the docs repo following templates.
2) Create a PR targeting docs-staging branch with title prefixed: [Docs] <short summary>.
3) CI checks (required):
   - Markdown/JSON schema validation
   - Code snippet linters (python -m flake8, npm run lint, go vet)
   - Link checker for internal and external links (fail on 4xx/5xx)
   - Spellcheck (tech-terms whitelist)
4) Reviewers: at least one SDK owner and one Docs editor must approve.
5) Staging deploy: PR merge triggers staging docs deploy. Author must sanity-check rendered page within 30 minutes.
6) Release window: weekly scheduled release on Tuesdays 09:00 PT; critical fixes can be hotfixed outside window with on-call approval.
7) Post-publish steps: update the changelog entry and notify #docs-release Slack channel with summary and affected pages.

Rollback / Emergency procedure:
1) If post-publish regression discovered (broken code example, invalid auth instructions, or missing required steps), create an emergency PR that reverts or fixes the change and mark as "emergency-fix" in the title.
2) Ping on-call Docs engineer and SRE if the fix affects authentication flows or rate-limits.
3) After merge, run smoke tests and confirm action by QA and support.

Versioning and deprecation policy for examples and SDK guides:
- Major breaking changes must have a migration guide and a deprecation window of at least 60 days with clear upgrade steps.
- Tag docs with stability: stable | deprecated | experimental.
- Deprecated examples must include a pointer to the replacement and a sunset date.

Top support issues (Q3 2025 — Q1 2026) and canonical fixes:
1) Issue: "SDK auth fails with 401 in some environments"
   Symptoms: Users report 401s when API key is set via environment variables in containerized builds.
   Root cause: CI build process strips environment variables during multi-stage builds; examples used os.environ directly with no fallback.
   Canonical fix: Update quickstarts to show both env var and config-file approaches; add note about multi-stage Docker builds and recommended ARG pass-through. Include checklist item to test examples in a minimal container.
   Related pages: sdk-python-guide-2026, quickstart-embeddings-python-2026
2) Issue: "Streaming responses hang or return partial transcripts"
   Symptoms: Large prompt streaming stalls after first chunk on Node examples.
   Root cause: Example uses an older HTTP client config that buffers responses and lacks proper chunk handling for transfer-encoding: chunked.
   Canonical fix: Update Node and curl examples to demonstrate the streaming client with backpressure-safe read loop. Add an integration test that asserts continuous chunks for a 4k token prompt.
3) Issue: "Embeddings mismatch between SDKs (different vector norms)"
   Symptoms: Customers compare embeddings generated from Python and Go SDKs and see subtle cosine-similarity differences.
   Root cause: One SDK normalized vectors client-side; the other left raw model outputs.
   Canonical fix: Standardize on returning raw vectors and document normalization recommendations in the SDK guide with sample code for normalization (numpy / gonum examples). Add a unit test that compares outputs for identical inputs across SDKs.
4) Issue: "Code snippets fail lint checks in CI"
   Symptoms: PRs blocked by code linter errors in snippet validation job.
   Root cause: Snippets were copied from REPL outputs and include trailing prompts or non-portable imports.
   Canonical fix: Enforce snippet hygiene: runnable, pinned dependencies, and include snippet CI job that executes each snippet in an isolated environment. Add a docs template header requiring a snippet test matrix.
5) Issue: "Outdated API parameters in quickstarts after model update"
   Symptoms: Quickstart examples reference removed parameter names and cause 400 errors.
   Root cause: Lack of automated breaking-change notification into docs pipeline.
   Canonical fix: Add a model-change webhook that opens a tracking issue and flags affected examples. Create a weekly audit job that runs smoke requests for quickstarts and records any 4xx/5xx responses as follow-ups.

Canonical triage process for new support issues referencing docs or examples:
1) Triage owner (Support engineer) files an issue in the docs tracker and assigns severity (P0: blocking; P1: high-impact; P2: medium).
2) Docs engineer reproduces and links failing snippet or doc section.
3) For P0/P1, author a hotfix PR and request expedited review; for P2 schedule in next docs sprint.
4) After fix, close support ticket with root cause and user-facing note; update the canonical fixes list.

CI and test matrix for examples (minimum):
- Python snippets: run in isolated venv, pytest smoke test, flake8
- Node snippets: run with npm ci and node --check, eslint
- Go snippets: go vet + go test (small harness)
- Curl: run with --fail and validate JSON output with jq
- Cross-language parity test: run a canonical input through all SDKs and compare response status and key fields (not necessarily 1:1 token outputs)

Documentation metrics and priorities:
- Priority areas: quickstarts, auth, streaming, embeddings, function-calling
- KPIs: time-to-first-success (tracked by quickstart runs in sample app telemetry), docs-related support tickets, snippet CI pass rate 
- Monthly review: maintainers review top 10 support issues and close or escalate as needed

Appendix: Useful commands and helper scripts
- Local snippet test runner: scripts/run_snippet_tests.sh (runs enabled snippet tests across languages)
- Link checker: scripts/check_links.sh (uses htmlproofer for built site or linkinator for JSON)
- Docs release: scripts/docs_release.sh --staging | --prod

Related resources:
- Developer Experience Docs Playbook: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/developer-experience-docs-playbook-2026
- SDK repo templates: github.com/redwood-inference/devex-sdk-templates
- Docs CI: github.com/redwood-inference/docs/.github/workflows/docs-ci.yml

Contact and support:
- Primary channel: #devex-docs on Slack
- Pager (on-call for emergency doc regressions): see eng-developer-experience on-call rota
